Using the cross product magnitude formula,

\[
\|\mathbf a \times \mathbf b\|=\|\mathbf a\|\|\mathbf b\|\sin\theta
\]

where \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf b\).

First compute

\[
\|\mathbf a \times \mathbf b\|
=
\left\|\begin{pmatrix}3\\2\\6\end{pmatrix}\right\|
=
\sqrt{3^2+2^2+6^2}
=
\sqrt{49}
=
7.
\]

Thus

\[
7=(2)(7)\sin\theta
\]

so

\[
\sin\theta=\frac12.
\]

Since the angle between two vectors is between \(0^\circ\) and \(180^\circ\), the possible angles are

\[
\theta=30^\circ \quad \text{or} \quad \theta=150^\circ.
\]

The smallest possible angle is therefore

\[
\boxed{30^\circ}
\]
